_comment: Synthetic example matching the support triage worked example. Scores are illustrative and were chosen before any ROI figure was calculated, per the scoring discipline.

requires_judgement.reason: Ticket intent is expressed in free text and often spans more than one category; the existing rules-based router misclassifies roughly a fifth of tickets.

unstructured_inputs.reason: Tickets arrive by email, web form, and chat, written by customers in their own words.

imperfect_answer_useful.reason: A drafted reply that an agent reviews before sending is useful even when it needs editing.

human_can_recover.reason: Every drafted reply passes a support agent before it reaches the customer, and misroutes are visible within one queue cycle.

justifications.judgement_required: Classification needs context weighing, though routing once classified is a lookup and should stay deterministic.
justifications.input_variability: Free-form customer text from three uncontrolled channels.
justifications.tolerance_for_error: Drafts are reviewed, so an imperfect draft is useful; billing disputes are the exception and are excluded from drafting.
justifications.recoverability: Review catches errors before they reach customers, but a misroute can delay a ticket by a day before anyone notices.
justifications.volume: About 4,000 tickets a month, enough that handling time dominates the support cost.
justifications.stability: Product changes shift the category mix roughly quarterly, so the classifier will need periodic re-evaluation.
